name: Meshach/Mishael
title: The Faithful in the Fire
summary: Mishael, who received the Babylonian name Meshach, was one of four young Jewish men taken to Babylon during Nebuchadnezzar's first conquest of Jerusalem. He is best known for his unwavering faith when, together with Shadrach and Abednego, he refused to worship King Nebuchadnezzar's golden statue and was thrown into the blazing furnace, where they were miraculously saved.

keyEvents.title: Exile to Babylon
keyEvents.description: Mishael, along with Daniel, Hananiah, and Azariah, was chosen from among the young nobles of Judah to serve at the Babylonian court. There he received the new name Meshach.

keyEvents.title: Refused to Eat the King's Food
keyEvents.description: Together with his three friends, Mishael refused to defile himself with the king's food and drink, choosing instead to eat only vegetables and water.

keyEvents.title: God's Gift of Wisdom
keyEvents.description: God gave the four young men knowledge and understanding in all literature and wisdom, and the king found them ten times wiser than all his wise men.

keyEvents.title: Appointed to an official position
keyEvents.description: After Daniel's interpretation of Nebuchadnezzar's dream, Meshach, Shadrach, and Abednego were appointed to govern the province of Babylon.

keyEvents.title: Refused to worship the golden statue
keyEvents.description: When Nebuchadnezzar erected a golden statue and commanded worship, Meshach and his two friends refused to bow down, even under threat of death in the fiery furnace.

keyEvents.title: Saved from the fiery furnace
keyEvents.description: God sent His angel to protect the three men in the seven times heated furnace. They came out unharmed, without even the smell of smoke, and the king praised their God.
